note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BAH 6(1)(a); A06b BAH 6(1)(a); L05 BAH 9(1)(a), 7(1); BAH 8(c), 7(2)): ordinary naturalisation after 25 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Bahrain, 2024
sources.said: Person has resided in the country for 25 years. ... n.a. ... Person has voluntarily acquired another citizenship without prior permission and an order is issued by His Majesty the Governor to withdraw the person's citizenship. Except if person acquired one of the nationalities of the Member States of the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf. Art. 7(1) talks explicitly about female citizens who acquires the citizenship of her foreign spouse.; Person is a naturalised citizen and retrieves his original citizenship without obtaining the prior permission of the Minister of Interior. Except if the person holds one of the nationalities of the Member States of the Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf. Art. 7(2) talks explicitly about female naturalised citizens who acquired the Bahraini citizenship as a spouse of a male citizen, who retrieves her original citizenship after marriage ties are broken.
